Commit the log plus the validator output. For the UI, show Wi-Fi off in the live demo; Chromium inside sandbox-exec is unverified.

findings.title: Context size and engine flags must be explicit and held constant per slot
findings.failure_scenario: Defaults are -c 0 (model's 262,144), --fit on, -ngl auto, -fa auto and 5 threads. Measured: -c 16384 -np 2 logged n_ctx_slot=8192 with kv_unified=false, so moving from 1 to 2 slots with the same -c halves each slot's context. A 3-turn case with prefetch could overflow or truncate in F only, showing up as a quality loss blamed on the wrong change. KV size also changes memory, which confounds the RAM comparison.
findings.change: Pin explicit -c, -np, -kvu or --kv-unified-per-slot, -ngl 99, -fa, -t, -b/-ub, --jinja, --reasoning off (plus enable_thinking:false), --cache-ram and --ctx-checkpoints in every profile, so per-slot context is identical across profiles. Record the server's own startup log values (n_ctx_slot, kv_unified, n_threads) into configuration. Log max prompt tokens per role per run, and fail closed (decision error with an actionable message) if a prompt exceeds 85% of per-slot context.

findings.title: Output tokens dominate cached steps; remove free-text fields the code already knows
findings.failure_scenario: With prefixes cached, a step is about 0.1 s prefill and 0.6–1.2 s decode at ~70 tok/s (44–86 tokens). The Ops 'summary' was 63–86 tokens (~1.2 s) per invocation, and in the probe it hallucinated 'Proposal P-0001 executed successfully' with no execute call. The R reply claimed 'Your refund of $30.00 ... has been processed' when nothing had executed. Each extra free-text field costs latency and opens another channel for invented success.
findings.change: report_to_resolution takes {outcome, reason_codes} only. The orchestrator builds the handoff result for Resolution from the structured OpsReport and store facts. Set per-request max_tokens to fit the tool (for example 96, and 160 for reply_to_customer). Keep tool and parameter names short but descriptive. Measure as an ablation 'structured ops report': expect fewer completion tokens per task and unchanged success. This is the most defensible quality-preserving optimization, because it removes hallucination surface while saving time.

findings.title: 'Context prefetch' is undefined and can break auditability, grounding and the 'meaningful agent use' requirement
findings.failure_scenario: If prefetch silently injects all of the customer's lines, or worse, eligibility verdicts, into the prompt, then: the action_audit no longer shows how the target was found; gate 2 may count prefetched IDs as 'grounded'; prompts grow with order count (large-account variants overflow context); and reviewers see the agents reduced to a script. Placing it before the stable prefix also kills cache reuse.
findings.change: Define prefetch as a deterministic, audited orchestrator call (agent 'orchestrator', tool 'prefetch_customer_lines', arguments plus result in action_audit). Scope it to the authenticated customer, cap it at N lines with a 'more available' flag, include line facts only (no eligibility verdicts), and append it after the system prompt and tools in the user turn. Grounding still uses customer text only. Report LLM calls per task with prefetch on and off, and confirm success is unchanged on variants that include many orders.

findings.title: Qwen3.5's template re-renders past assistant turns differently, so the cache prefix breaks at every new user turn
findings.failure_scenario:
The template wraps assistant messages after the last user query in '<think>

</think>

' and renders earlier ones without it. When turn N+1's user message arrives, turn N's assistant tool calls are re-rendered differently, and the hybrid model (qwen35: SSM layers with full attention every 4th layer) falls back to its last checkpoint. Measured: cache_n 1200 with 283 tokens re-prefilled. With --checkpoint-min-step defaulting to 8192, mid-prompt checkpoints are rare, so longer histories lose more.
findings.change: Per turn, rebuild a compact context (system plus tools, then the case-state digest, then the current message) instead of replaying the full transcript; prior turns become a deterministic structured summary. Or pass reasoning_content:'' consistently. Declare --ctx-checkpoints and --checkpoint-min-step, and report the cached-token ratio per turn index, so the effect is visible.

findings.title: Tests and evidence for top architecture marks: independent oracle, metamorphic suite, adversarial FakeLLM
findings.failure_scenario: If evals/ imports desk.policy, every 'success' is circular. If only the 6 public cases are tested, hardcoding (C100/O100/L1/TEE) cannot be ruled out, and private variants will find it. Without tests showing that the gates hold when the LLM misbehaves, the claim that money, authorization and invariants live in deterministic code cannot be defended in Q&A.
findings.change: (1) evals/oracle.py: an independent ~100-line implementation of the disclosed rules that does not import desk. Hypothesis differential tests compare oracle and policy on random states, covering 0/30/31-day boundaries, month ends and leap years. (2) Metamorphic suite: rename every ID and SKU, shift all dates by k days, and paraphrase messages; outcomes must be invariant. (3) Adversarial FakeLLM scripts: execute without a grant, execute twice, wrong line, invented success text, parallel calls, malformed args, budget exhaustion, re-execute after TIMEOUT. Assert final-state invariants: stock ≥ 0, refund sum ≤ paid, ≤1 transaction per request_id, quarantine never sellable. (4) A test that adapter and UI build the same Session object. (5) scripts/check.sh runs unit tests, the adapter with FakeLLM on public and variants, the validator and the offline check. (6) A reset command (scripts/reset.sh, plus POST /reset) with a test that state after reset is byte-identical to the fixture. (7) Commit early and often; the repo currently has zero commits.

findings.title: Speculative decoding: tested once, result inconclusive, so present it as a proposal
findings.failure_scenario: --spec-type draft-simple with the local Qwen3.5-0.8B-Q8_0 draft produced byte-identical tool calls (lossless at temperature 0) with 82% draft acceptance (235/285). Speed was mixed: prefill 1,191 ms vs 817 ms, some steps 88 tok/s vs 70, and later steps 37–40 tok/s while the other server was running. It costs about 0.8 GB more. Claiming it without a controlled ablation would be unsupported.
findings.change: Either run it as a proper leave-one-out ablation under the hygiene rules, or list it on the 'proposed, not measured' slide next to an ngram/prompt-lookup variant. The brief requires measured results and proposals kept apart.

findings.title: Make every slide number traceable to a file and declare determinism
findings.failure_scenario: Numbers typed into slides by hand, missing raw logs, or 'seed 42' without noting that greedy decoding ignores it all invite 'how do I reproduce this?' questions that cost presentation and evidence points.
findings.change: Per run: results/<profile>/run-<k>/{results.json, validate.txt, server.log, metrics_before/after.prom, run_conditions.json, argv.txt}. report.py writes results/REPORT.md plus CSVs, and every slide figure cites its file and command. configuration.seed reads 42 and notes that temperature 0 makes decoding greedy, so the seed does not affect it. Record a per-case decision-trace hash and report how many of the 3 runs were identical. One slide for measured results, one for proposed improvements, one for limitations (AGX figure is system-wide, small n, no true-cold sample without sudo, sandbox-exec is deprecated, Q4 quality checked only on our variant suite).

clarification_questions.question: On Apple unified memory, should metrics.peak_vram_mb hold the measured GPU-attributable unified memory (Metal/IOAccelerator allocation), or null with a separate unified-memory field?
clarification_questions.default_assumption: Report the measured value (AGXAccelerator 'In use system memory' delta over idle) in peak_vram_mb, mirror it in peak_unified_gpu_mb, and add memory_architecture:'unified' with a note that it overlaps peak_ram_mb and must not be added to it.
clarification_questions.why_default: The validator accepts a number or null. A number meets 'record peak accelerator memory', and the note meets 'explain limitations'. Null tells an automated grader the metric is unavailable when it can in fact be measured.

clarification_questions.question: Does 'run every public scenario 3 times from a clean initial state' also require a fresh inference server / cleared prompt caches per run or per case, or only reset business state?
clarification_questions.default_assumption: Reset business state before every case. Start a fresh adapter and llama-server process per run (3 cold starts per profile). The prompt cache persists within a run and is declared. Add a supplementary ablation with a server restart per case.
clarification_questions.why_default: This passes both the strict and the lenient reading, gives cold-start samples, and keeps warm numbers realistic and declared.

clarification_questions.question: Is 'complete-task success' and p50/p95 latency measured per case (all turns) or per turn, and are generated IDs and response wording ignored?
clarification_questions.default_assumption: Per case. Success requires every turn's decision and the final business state to match, ignoring candidate-generated IDs and wording. Latency is case elapsed_ms excluding server startup. Per-turn and per-step latency are secondary.
clarification_questions.why_default: It matches the 'complete-task' wording and the per-case metrics object in the contract, and it is the strictest reading, so we cannot be accused of inflating success.

clarification_questions.question: Is changing quantization (Q8_0 baseline → Q4_K_M final) accepted as an optimization if quality is shown to be preserved, or should baseline and final use the same model file?
clarification_questions.default_assumption: Allowed. We also publish a same-quant (Q4_K_M) baseline→final comparison and break the headline speedup down by change.
clarification_questions.why_default: Both readings are covered, and the 'deliberately weak baseline' penalty cannot apply because the engineering-only gain is shown on its own.

clarification_questions.question: Will evaluators run `python adapter.py` themselves (on which machine, with which Python and llama.cpp), or will we run it on our device during the session?
clarification_questions.default_assumption: It runs on our device. adapter.py is a stdlib shim that re-execs the project venv and auto-starts the pinned llama-server. Setup for another Apple Silicon Mac is documented; other platforms are declared unsupported.
clarification_questions.why_default: `python` does not exist on PATH here, so the literal command must work through the shim no matter who types it.

clarification_questions.question: Should peak_ram_mb include the separate inference-server process, or only the adapter process?
clarification_questions.default_assumption: Include both: the sum of kernel high-water phys_footprint for the adapter process tree and llama-server, with a per-process breakdown and RSS shown alongside.
clarification_questions.why_default: Leaving out the server would understate memory by several GB and look like gaming; including it with a breakdown is transparent.

clarification_questions.question: Does the injected timeout_after_commit count toward 'failures and timeouts', and what decision is expected on the timed-out turn: completed after reconciliation, or error?
clarification_questions.default_assumption: Injected faults are reported separately from real timeouts. The turn is 'completed' only if reconciliation verifies the committed transaction in the store; otherwise 'error'. The replay turn is 'completed' with no new effects.
clarification_questions.why_default: This follows CONTRACT ('recovery must query/reconcile') and 'never invent a successful transaction', and keeps the failure counts honest.

clarification_questions.question: Is a sandbox-exec network-deny run (loopback allowed) acceptable proof of offline execution, or must the live demo show networking physically disabled?
clarification_questions.default_assumption: Both: a committed sandboxed adapter run with a negative-control check, and Wi-Fi off during the live UI demo.
clarification_questions.why_default: The sandbox run is reproducible by a reviewer; the live demo covers the UI and browser path, which the sandbox does not.

clarification_questions.question: May we run more than 3 repetitions per scenario for tighter percentiles, or must the reported numbers be exactly 3 runs?
clarification_questions.default_assumption: The headline table uses exactly 3 runs, as the brief specifies. Extra runs and per-step distributions are supplementary and labelled.
clarification_questions.why_default: Results stay directly comparable with the other candidate while still giving statistically meaningful tails.

clarification_questions.question: How large can private variants get: number of turns, orders and lines per customer, and could other customers' orders appear in initial_state?
clarification_questions.default_assumption: Up to about 6 turns and about 20 order lines, with other customers' orders present. Context is sized with 2x headroom, and an overflow fails closed with an actionable error.
clarification_questions.why_default: Context budget and prefetch caps depend on this; failing closed never invents a transaction.

Large account (about 12 orders × 3 lines, several TEE-M lines across orders): 'Refund line L2 of order O107' → propose exactly that line, then completed; the generic 'refund my medium tee' → clarify. Exercises the prefetch cap and per-slot context headroom without changing correctness.
